chapter: Tom Albert and Baton Rouge bands
title: Toots Johnson's band personnel and the fatal car accident
summary: Handy names the leading bands outside New Orleans and Toots Johnson's sidemen, then tells of a crash that killed bassist Mal.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: And he'd sing a lot of them. Did a lot of singing. But he didn't play anything. Oh, he had a playhouse in his yard, though. That thing was around 12 by 12 was a little girl. He had a real funny to play. He was a great guy. He was a great guy. for his little girl. They had real furniture in there too, but that was just the playhouse there. He had a wonderful home over there. Well, there was the three leading orchestras outside of New Orleans. It was Bud Scott, Claiborne William, and Tut Johnson. Claiborne William out of Donaldsonville, Tut Johnson out of Baton Rouge, and Bud Scott out of Natchez. Well, they was doing all the business out there, and I was with Tut. And I stayed with Tut from 24 until 26. Then I left Tut and went with the Tony Harris. Who was with Tut at that time? Tut Johnson had at that time Clarence Thompson on drum, Euless Jarrou on trumpet, Dimes on

A little Wesley Dimes. He's dead now. He got killed. And he had Robert. They called him Bob. He plays around here. He plays on the, he's kind of sick now. He waits down here at the first precinct. You know Bob. He played trombone. So he recorded with, uh... Bob Thomas? Yeah. He recorded with Bob Ryan. He recorded with several orchestra friends. Yeah. But he was playing trombone at the time.
And is he from Baton Rouge or something? I think Bob is from Baton Rouge. He's out in California now, you know. Is he? Yeah.
Yeah. I thought he was still working downtown.
No, I want to see him if I get out there. Oh yeah. Well, Tut was a guitar player. Tut Johnson,

he was a guitar player. He was playing guitar. He had a fella by the name of Mal playing bass. Now I got killed. One night, we was coming from White Castle. A fella dropped and ran into our car and hit the back wheel and turned us over. And, uh, turned us over three times in the middle of the street. And I was sitting right side of Mal. We was sitting on that side and I was sitting in the middle. And along the build tunnel and busted his bass all up. Killed him. Didn't kill him right. Then we take him to a black man to a hospital. And when he got there, he was dead.
